headline: Stocks surged Monday (S&P 500 +2.35%, best day since April), and now all eyes are on October CPI at 8:30 ET, with December hike odds above 80% and Waller floating 50bp if core is hot.
regime: Hiking regime with a sharp relief rally: the Fed raised rates in September, December hike odds are 82% (CME FedWatch via Hawksmoor), the 10-year is about 4.88%, and the VIX is near 20 after 28 on Nov 5. A hot core CPI would test the rebound.

lean.why: S&P futures are flat (+0.06%) and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.24% after Monday's 2.35% gain. CPI is at 8:30 ET, the 10-year auction at 1 pm and CoreWeave after the close.
PPI (Nov 13), Nvidia earnings (Nov 17) and the Dec 8-9 FOMC are ahead; hike odds above 80% keep yields in focus.
The Nasdaq was still about 11% below its Oct 6 record on Friday; a hiking Fed and data-center regulation worries are real risks.

rates.n: Held Oct 28; next meeting Dec 8-9 (older reading, no new decision)
Freddie Mac survey of Nov 5 (older; next release Thursday Nov 12)
19.94 early Tuesday (Hawksmoor; Monday close not labeled); 28.18 on Nov 5

sectors.why: (Nov 9 read.) First Solar fell about 5% Monday as oil dropped; all sectors rose in the broad rally.
(Nov 5-9 read.) Moderna closed Nov 9 at $269.00 (+5.83%) on its first profitable quarter in two years; Ionis fell about 21% on a guidance cut.
(Nov 4 read, not updated.) Lockheed -7%, L3Harris -6%; Boeing plans about 5% staff cuts (TheStreet, Nov 9). Industrials led Monday, up 4.59%.
AMD +13.26% to $508.58, Broadcom +8.78% and Micron +6.25% to $733.15 on Monday; Nvidia -4.27% to $178.67 on its CEO probe. Nvidia reports Nov 17.
(Nov 9 read.) A hiking Fed helps margins but raises credit worries; no new bank-specific news found today.
(Nov 9 read.) The 10-year near 4.88% and a 7.18% mortgage rate remain headwinds; CPI and the next mortgage survey (Nov 12) are the tests.
Gold rose 1.74% to $4,138 Monday and was about $4,074 early Tuesday; the CPI print and hike odds are the swing factors.
WTI is about $85 (-2%) and Brent $90 early Tuesday, about 23% below Brent's Oct 30 high of $118, as Trump says new Iran strikes are unlikely; the blockade continues.
The Russell 2000 rose 3.15% to 2,840.81 on Monday (TheStreet); hike odds above 80% are a headwind for borrowers.
(Nov 9 read.) Tesla rose about 5% Monday on robotaxi expansion (Yahoo).
Constellation closed Nov 9 at $276.09 (+10.46%) after a Q3 beat and a raised outlook; NRG rose 10.45% on a $4B plant sale.
(Nov 4 read, not updated.) GEO -6.7% and CoreCivic -5.2% on the new Congress.

news.head: Fed's Waller leans to a 25bp December hike, would consider 50bp if CPI is hot
news.srcN: Yahoo Finance live blog, Nov 10; Hawksmoor Capital, Nov 10
news.mean: Gov. Waller (speaking in London) said a 25bp hike is his lean for December but that 50bp 'should be considered' if core CPI is around 0.3% or higher. FedWatch odds of a December hike are over 80% (82.2% per Hawksmoor).
react: Hot CPI plus a 50bp talk raises the risk of a higher yield
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a Fed official floating a bigger move before a data print raises the stakes of that print.
news.today: Waller's remarks and the 8:30 ET CPI are the two catalysts; stay small into the data.
news.later: A hiking cycle is a rate-and-valuation story; investors tend to watch core inflation and the Dec 8-9 meeting.

news.head: October CPI at 8:30 ET: consensus +0.3% headline, +0.2% core
news.mean: Consensus is +0.3% headline and +0.2% core month over month; September was +0.6% and +0.3%. There is no year-over-year figure because October 2025 data were not collected during the shutdown.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: markets rarely move on in-line prints; the surprise in core matters more than the headline.
news.today: S&P futures were flat (+0.06%) and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.24% before the print.
news.later: One print rarely changes the long-term view; the trend over several months does.

news.head: Stocks surge Monday: S&P 500 +2.35%, Nasdaq +2.74%, Russell 2000 +3.15%
news.mean: The S&P 500 had its best day since Apr 8 (SPY +2.37%, QQQ +3.54%, IWM +3.23%), the Dow rose 1,104 points to about 52,390, and 75% of stocks rose with industrials leading. Drivers named include a drop in oil after Trump said new Iran strikes were unlikely, a chip rebound and Citi moving US stocks and global tech to neutral.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: after a 4.4% one-day drop on Nov 5, sharp rebounds can retrace; the hike-odds backdrop has not changed.
news.today: Watch whether the bounce holds after CPI.
news.later: The Nasdaq was about 11% below its Oct 6 record on Friday (Yahoo); a bounce does not remove the rate and regulation risks.

news.head: Oil falls: WTI about $85, Brent $90, as Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely
news.srcN: Hawksmoor Capital, Nov 10; TheStreet and Stocktitan, Nov 9
news.mean: WTI was $84.99 (-2.1%) and Brent $90.23 (-2.5%) early Tuesday, about 23% below Brent's Oct 30 high of $118. Trump said military action 'doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing' while the naval blockade continues; Waller said Hormuz insurance and ship transfers add $20-30 a barrel.
react: Fell about 5% Monday on lower oil
news.hist: Rule of thumb: oil headlines about Iran can reverse within hours.
news.today: Crude is headline-driven; the blockade is unresolved.
news.later: Lower oil eases the inflation worry, but Iran news can reverse it.

news.head: Chips rebound: AMD +13.3%, Broadcom +8.8%; Nvidia -4.3% on the CEO probe
news.mean: AMD closed at $508.58 (+13.26%) after an Oppenheimer upgrade, Broadcom rose 8.78%, and Taiwan's main index rose 4.94%. Nvidia fell 4.27% to $178.67 after its board opened an investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang; Nvidia reports Nov 17.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: mega-cap governance headlines can move the whole Nasdaq-100; facts are still emerging.
news.today: Nvidia is up about 1.3% premarket (Hawksmoor); watch for probe updates.
news.later: Chips remain volatile; Nvidia's Nov 17 report is the next fundamental test.

news.head: Constellation Energy +10.5% on a Q3 beat and raised 2026 guidance
news.srcN: Yahoo Finance, Nov 9; Alpha Vantage close
news.mean: Constellation closed at $276.09 (+10.46%) after adjusted EPS of $5.06 vs about $3.90 expected and a raised full-year outlook.
react: Power group read-through; NRG +10.45% on a $4B plant sale
news.hist: Rule of thumb: power and nuclear names trade on data-center demand and regulation headlines.
news.today: Strong one-day moves can fade; watch follow-through.
news.later: AI power demand vs possible data-center limits is the theme.

news.head: Earnings movers: Telos +48.8%, Delcath +35.8%, Ionis -21%; Rocket Lab down after hours
news.mean: Telos rose 48.76% on a raised 2026 forecast, Delcath 35.77% on Q3 revenue of $35.1M, Ionis fell about 21% after cutting its 2026 Tryngolza sales forecast to about $50M. After hours Rocket Lab fell 6.66% despite record $268M revenue, and Trade Desk rose as much as 26% before fading.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: earnings gaps often fade within days when guidance details are thin.
news.today: After-hours moves can reverse by the open.
news.later: Judge results over several quarters, not one gap.

news.head: 10-year yield about 4.88%; $42B 10-year auction at 1 pm; bond market shut Wednesday
news.mean: The 10-year yield was 4.884% early Tuesday (4.864% on Yahoo's blog). A $42B 10-year note auction is at 1 pm ET, the 30-year auction is Thursday and the bond market is closed Wednesday for Veterans Day.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: weak auction demand can push yields up even without data surprises.
news.today: Auction results land at 1 pm ET, after CPI.
news.later: Yields near 4.9% keep mortgage rates high.

news.head: 30-year mortgage rate 7.18%, third straight weekly decline; next survey Thursday
news.mean: Freddie Mac's 30-year rate was 7.18% vs 7.24% the prior week and 6.22% a year ago; the 15-year was 6.57%. The next survey is due Thursday Nov 12.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: mortgage rates follow the 10-year yield with a short lag.
news.later: With the 10-year near 4.9%, a sustained drop in mortgage rates needs lower yields.

news.head: Gold $4,138 Monday (+1.74%), about $4,074 early Tuesday
news.srcN: Yahoo Finance, Nov 9; Hawksmoor Capital, Nov 10
news.mean: Gold rose 1.74% to $4,138.25 Monday, then traded near $4,074 (-1.6%) early Tuesday as the dollar index held about 101.7.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gold tends to weaken when real yields and hike odds rise.
news.today: A hot CPI is the main downside risk.
news.later: Gold is a hedge, not a yield asset, with rates high.

news.head: October payrolls +165k vs about 65k expected; unemployment 4.1%
news.mean: Payrolls rose 165,000 (consensus cited at 59k-70k), unemployment was 4.1% vs 4.2% expected, and wages rose 0.4% m/m vs 0.3%. August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000, and the three-month average is 137,000.
react: Mixed: margins up, growth outlook better
Gold fell 0.94% as the dollar rose
news.hist: Rule of thumb: strong jobs data in a hiking regime lifts rate expectations, which usually helps the dollar and pressures gold and housing.
news.today: The data is old news by Monday; focus has shifted to CPI.
news.later: The Fed has raised once this cycle, and another hike is now the market's base case; investors weigh rate risk in rate-sensitive holdings.

news.head: Democrats win Congress; AI data-center rules and tariff relief are the market's two read-throughs
news.mean: Investors fear rules on AI data centers; Goldman estimates about 45% of planned US data-center capacity faces possible restrictions (Yahoo). On the other side, homebuilders rallied (NVR up more than 26% premarket) because UBS says Democratic control could improve the odds of lower tariffs on building materials.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy surprises are often priced fast, then re-priced as the details emerge.
news.today: State-level data-center headlines can move the group in minutes.
news.later: Divided government usually slows big new laws; permits and power rules are the practical risk.

calendar.t: October CPI (8:30 ET); 10-year auction (1 pm); Waller speaks; CoreWeave after the close
calendar.usual: Consensus headline +0.3%, core +0.2%; core matters most for December's hike. CoreWeave consensus EPS -$1.53 on $3.54B revenue.

calendar.t: Veterans Day: bond market closed, stocks open
calendar.usual: Thin Treasury trading; no major US data.

calendar.t: Freddie Mac mortgage rates; 30-year auction; Nebius, Cisco, Applied Materials earnings
calendar.usual: AI infrastructure read-through; the last survey was 7.18%.
Follows CPI; can move yields if it surprises.
Corporate buybacks often support stocks after blackout periods end.
Sets the tone for AI chips and the Nasdaq-100.

out: Relief; focus moves to Nebius and Cisco

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
